business_scope.primary_industry_name: Vertical Industrial ERP and Customer Relationship Software

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Vanuatu (unitary national jurisdiction, no sub-state tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid - Common Law (Anglo-Australian heritage) with French Civil Law influence; unitary national jurisdiction without sub-state tax distinctions.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Member of the World Trade Organization (WTO) since 24 August 2012
Pacific Island Countries Trade Agreement (PICTA) - active regional free trade agreement
Melanesian Spearhead Group (MSG) Trade Agreement - active

No comprehensive double taxation avoidance agreement (DTAA) in force; jurisdiction operates a tax-exempt offshore regime for International Companies; limited Tax Information Exchange Agreements (TIEAs) with OECD partners are applied

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Governed by the International Companies Act [Cap. 222] (as amended) and the Anti-Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Act No. 36 of 2012 (as amended), together with subsidiary AML/CFT regulations and directives issued by the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) and the Vanuatu Financial Intelligence Unit (VFIU). Beneficial ownership information must be identified, verified and maintained in the confidential register held by the licensed registered agent and must be available on lawful demand to VFSC, VFIU and Vanuatu law enforcement authorities.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory application of customer due diligence and beneficial ownership identification under the Vanuatu AML/CFT Act (No. 36 of 2012) and FATF Recommendations 10, 12, 22 and 24. The licensed registered agent must screen all directors, shareholders, UBOs and controlling persons against PEP databases, the UN Consolidated Sanctions List and domestic Vanuatu sanctions instruments. As a market prerequisite for USD-denominated Stripe Billing and Direct Debit payment rails, OFAC SDN List screening and negative adverse-media checks are applied on an ongoing basis. The engagement is risk-rated as Low_Risk_Standard for ISIC 6201 software/ERP/CRM export services, with simplified but mandatory ongoing transaction monitoring.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) - Companies and International Companies Registry; name clearance is submitted by the licensed registered agent through the VFSC corporate registration platform.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names are accepted in Latin-script English, French or Bislama, the three official languages of Vanuatu; no separate transliteration script is mandated. An International Company must bear its full name in Latin characters and must end with 'Limited', 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Societe Anonyme' (S.A.), or a permitted abbreviation. Names identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered entity, names implying connection with the Government of Vanuatu, and names misleadingly suggesting a regulated activity are disallowed under section 8 of the International Companies Act [Cap. 222].
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon VFSC rejection of a proposed name, the licensed registered agent files a written reconsideration submission with the Registrar of International Companies within 14 days of the refusal notice, articulating distinctiveness, proposing spelling variations and removing offending tokens. If the administrative reconsideration is refused, the applicant resubmits a fresh primary and secondary name through the registered agent. A further administrative review may be requested from the VFSC Commissioner, and the Registrar's final decision is subject to judicial review before the Supreme Court of Vanuatu. A rejected name may not be reused in consecutive applications within the reservation window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Fully permissible. An International Company is not required to maintain physical trading premises in Vanuatu. The statutory registered office under section 10 of the International Companies Act [Cap. 222] is the address of the licensed registered agent, where the company records, member register and UBO register are maintained. The ISIC 6201 vertical ERP/CRM cloud business may operate entirely remotely, and a virtual office with mail forwarding is the market-standard solution. No business licence is required for this non-licensed software service activity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low - estimated annualized risk of an unannounced physical on-site inspection below 5% for a non-licensed, low-risk software/ICT offshore company with no in-country physical premises. Primary supervisory oversight is exercised over the licensed registered agent, which is subject to routine VFSC inspections and AML/CFT compliance reviews. If the company later establishes a physical office or employs staff in Vanuatu, inspection exposure rises accordingly.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act [Cap. 222], ss. 2–10 (formation and registration) and Part III (shares) — Republic of Vanuatu
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC), Companies Registry, Port Vila
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 — Application for Registration of an International Company (filed with the Memorandum and Articles of Association)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; authorized capital commonly set at USD 10,000 with a nominal paid-up subscription (as low as USD 1). No escrow account or bank attestation is required for incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the Company do hereby subscribe to the fully paid shares set forth in the subscription schedule appended hereto, and that the Directors record payment of the aggregate subscription proceeds into the Company's authorized corporate account. RESOLVED FURTHER that the registered office situated at the registered office address in Port Vila, Republic of Vanuatu, be and is hereby adopted as the statutory registered office for all purposes under the International Companies Act [Cap. 222], and that the registered agent be retained to maintain the statutory registers. RESOLVED FURTHER that [Name] be appointed President and [Name] be appointed Secretary, each to serve until the next annual meeting, with authority to execute banking instructions and filing instruments.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) — Companies Registry, Port Vila (in person or via VFSC e-portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a name reservation application listing three proposed names in order of preference. The Registry scans the International Companies register and rejects names that are identical or confusingly similar to an existing or reserved name. The cleared name is reserved for 21 days pending incorporation.
required_dossiers: Copy of applicant's passport and proof of address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected for resemblance, promptly re-file with an alternative name from the list, or request a written review of the Registrar's decision within 14 days pursuant to the Registry's administrative review procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: VFSC-licensed registered agent and a Vanuatu Notary Public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent prepares the Memorandum and Articles of Association, setting the authorized share capital and the company's objects for ISIC 6201 vertical ERP/CRM cloud software. The subscriber executes the instruments in the presence of a notary, who attests the signatures and seals the charter documents.
required_dossiers: Subscriber identity documents (passport and utility bill)
Letter of appointment of the registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any notarial deficiency is cured by re-executing the affected instrument before a licensed notary; the Registry accepts the corrected version with a fresh attestation date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Application for Registration of an International Company
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: VFSC Companies Registry — online submission through the VFSC licensed agent's e-dossier
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent lodges Form 1 together with the notarized charter documents, the directors' consents and the registered agent's consent, and pays the statutory registration fee (USD 250) by bank transfer or card. The application must declare that the company does not engage in domestic Vanuatu business.
required_dossiers: Form 1 — Application for Registration of an International Company
Declaration of each director consenting to act
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If queried, the registered agent responds within 14 days with corrected declarations or missing documents; the Registry re-assesses the amended filing within 3 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon satisfactory review, the Registrar assigns the company's unique registration number, endorses the charter, issues the Certificate of Incorporation, and registers the company in the International Companies register. The certificate is dispatched electronically to the registered agent, with a hard copy couriered to the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any clerical error in the certificate is corrected by a formal request to the Registrar attaching the certificate and a supporting board resolution; the Registrar issues a corrected certificate within 5 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of Registered Office and Appointment of Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: VFSC-licensed registered agent at a Port Vila address
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Pursuant to the first board resolution, the board adopts the Port Vila registered office and engages the registered agent. The agent files the Notice of Registered Office, updates the VFSC register, and takes custody of the statutory registers (members, directors, officers, charges).
required_dossiers: Registered agent consent and service agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar contests the address, file an amended Notice of Registered Office with a different compliant Port Vila address; the change is effective on acceptance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting, Share Subscription and Corporate Banking
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors; licensed commercial bank in Vanuatu or a correspondent offshore bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The directors convene the first board meeting and adopt the pro forma resolutions covering share subscription, registered office adoption and officer appointments. The secretary files the officer registers with the registered agent and presents the incorporation bundle to the bank for account opening and initial paid-up capital deposit.
required_dossiers: Passports of directors and authorized signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires further enhanced due diligence, supply certified corporate registers and a bank-approved director background statement; alternatively, engage a second licensed bank for the account opening.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) — sectoral industrial authorization not required for ISIC 6201; the IC Certificate of Incorporation constitutes the sole operating authorization.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — no statutory operating license is mandated for offshore vertical ERP/CRM cloud software under the International Companies Act [Cap. 222].

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Vanuatu Department of Environmental Protection and Conservation (DEPC), Ministry of Climate Change Adaptation, Meteorology and Geo-Hazards, Environment, Energy and Disaster Management
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no physical premises, manufacturing, or stationary emission sources; full EIA not required for pure software-as-a-service operations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable — zero on-site wastewater or VOC emissions; all infrastructure is cloud-hosted by third parties. Any minimal local waste (e.g., retired hardware) must comply with the Vanuatu Waste Management Act [Cap. 273] and WEEE handling standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable for a non-resident offshore IC with no physical workplace. Should a Vanuatu representative office be established, a fire safety certificate under the Fire Services Act [Cap. 82], a structural inspection certificate from the Public Works Department, and an occupational workplace clearance would then be required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Vanuatu Customs and Inland Revenue Authority (VCIRA), Port Vila, Republic of Vanuatu; created by the Tax and Customs (Administration) Reforms Act 2019 as a merger of the Department of Customs and the former Inland Revenue Department. Principal portal: www.vcira.vu (VCIRA Online Services) for VAT registration, VAT return submission, and customs entries; customs declarations are processed through the ASYCUDA World system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: A foreign beneficial owner engages a licensed registered agent in Vanuatu to incorporate an International Company (IC) under the International Companies Act [Cap. 222]. Step 2: The agent files the constitution, memorandum and articles, consent of first director, and registered office address with the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC); the Certificate of Incorporation and unique IC registration number are usually issued within 1-2 business days. Step 3: Because an IC is statutorily exempt from all national direct and indirect taxes on international business and is prohibited from carrying on domestic business with Vanuatu residents, no separate TIN or VAT ID is automatically created; the VFSC registration number serves as the corporate identity for all tax-exempt offshore activities. Step 4: If domestic VAT-taxable activity is ever undertaken, compulsory VAT registration applies within 21 days after the turnover threshold is exceeded, using VAT Form 100 submitted to VCIRA; VCIRA then issues a VAT registration number and certificate. Step 5: The IC must maintain a licensed registered agent in Vanuatu, file an annual return with the VFSC, and, if foreign-owned, hold a Foreign Investment Registration approval issued by the Vanuatu Investment Promotion Authority.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone: an International Company is wholly exempt from all Vanuatu national taxes on foreign-source business - no corporate income tax, no capital gains tax, no dividend, interest, royalty, or management-fee withholding tax, no inheritance or gift tax, and no stamp duty on offshore instruments. The exemption is conditioned on the IC carrying on business exclusively with non-residents and not holding an interest in land or engaging in domestic trade in Vanuatu. Pass-through concepts and entity-level income tax are inapplicable because Vanuatu imposes no income tax at either the entity or shareholder level; the territorial scope of the exemption is limited to offshore-source activities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election or hybrid-mismatch election exists in Vanuatu because the jurisdiction has no income tax and therefore generates no deduction, credit, or mismatch computations. Available elections under the International Companies Act: (1) conversion of an IC into a local 'ordinary company' under the Companies Act [Cap. 191] by special resolution and VFSC consent, which prospectively terminates the tax-exempt status and exposes the company to VAT, customs duty, and other obligations on local supplies; (2) an election in the constitutional documents to restrict the corporate objects to 'international business', which affirmatively preserves the exemption; and (3) optional voluntary VAT registration by an exporter to claim input VAT credits when below the compulsory threshold. None of these elections interact with hybrid mismatch rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Value Added Tax Act No. 9 of 1998 (as amended by the Value Added Tax (Amendment) Act 2025), administered by the Vanuatu Customs and Inland Revenue Authority (VCIRA); destination-based consumption tax with the standard headline rate increased from 12.5% to 15% effective 1 July 2025.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: VT 4,000,000 (Vanuatu Vatu, approximately USD 33,000): compulsory registration for any person carrying on a taxable activity in Vanuatu where the value of taxable supplies, including zero-rated supplies, reaches or exceeds VT 4,000,000 in any 12-month period; the VAT registration application (Form 100) must be submitted to VCIRA within 21 days of crossing the threshold. The International Company conducting pure offshore business is outside the domestic VAT net and is not required to register; voluntary registration is available to claim input VAT credits.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or continuous transaction control (CTC) e-invoicing regime is currently in force in Vanuatu. VAT-registered suppliers must issue a tax invoice containing the statutory particulars: supplier name and VAT registration number, recipient name, invoice date, description of the supply, VAT-exclusive price, VAT amount, and applicable rate. VAT returns are filed electronically through the VCIRA Online Services portal, and customs entries are lodged via ASYCUDA World. Fiscal digitalisation, including future e-invoicing standards for services suppliers, is under government review but has not been legislated for ERP/CRM cloud service providers.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supplier may claim the 0% VAT rate where the supply qualifies as an export of goods (removed from Vanuatu within 28 days of the date of invoice) or a supply of services to a non-resident customer for use and enjoyment wholly outside Vanuatu, per Section 6 and the Second Schedule of the Value Added Tax Act. For the vertical ERP/CRM cloud (SaaS) business, zero-rating is available when: (a) the customer is a non-resident; (b) the software is delivered electronically and accessed from servers or devices outside Vanuatu; (c) no Vanuatu-resident user obtains economic enjoyment of the service; and (d) payment is received in foreign currency through a licensed bank. Input VAT attributable to zero-rated export supplies is fully creditable, and excess credits are refundable through the periodic VAT return (Form 200). An International Company of Vanuatu is entirely outside the VAT charge on international business and may render services without charging Vanuatu VAT at all.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CED) validated in ASYCUDA World for physical goods or software media
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill (or electronic delivery acknowledgement for digital services)
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) issued by a licensed Vanuatu bank evidencing receipt of export proceeds in foreign currency
Commercial invoice and zero-rated VAT invoice issued to the non-resident buyer
Signed software license, SaaS subscription, or master services agreement evidencing offshore use, service delivery, and payment terms
Evidence of server location and offshore service delivery for cloud-based supplies
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: VCIRA conducts documentary and risk-based audits of zero-rated export claims and may recharacterize a supply as taxable in Vanuatu where contract performance, server usage, or customer enjoyment indicates local economic use. A false or unsupported zero-rating claim triggers a retrospective VAT assessment at 15% plus statutory late-payment interest, a 25% uplift for unreported tax understatement, and an accuracy or civil penalty of up to 100% of the tax evaded for deliberate conduct; knowingly issuing a false export invoice is a criminal offence carrying fines and imprisonment under the Value Added Tax Act. Refunded input VAT is clawed back with interest upon audit reversal. In addition, export proceeds must be repatriated through a licensed Vanuatu bank within 180 days of shipment or invoice date; failure to repatriate may result in disallowance of the zero-rating, exchange-control review, and anti-money-laundering referral.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of Vanuatu (RBV) acting pursuant to the Exchange Control Act [Cap 83] and operating through the Ministry of Finance and the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission for International Company remittances.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Vanuatu maintains a broadly liberal exchange control regime. The Vatu (VUV) is fully convertible for current account transactions and, for registered International Companies, capital account transactions are effectively unrestricted. An International Company is classified as a non-resident entity; it therefore may hold VUV or any foreign currency without Central Bank approval. Profit, capital and liquidation remittances to non-resident shareholders are freely payable, are free of withholding tax, and are not subject to dividend-blocking regulations, provided that all underlying revenue arises from non-resident business. Only residents or local trading companies are required to seek formal exchange control approval for certain foreign borrowings and large remissions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender or statutory conversion ratio applies to export proceeds earned by an International Company. Vanuatu does not impose repatriation deadlines or percentage-based conversion requirements on ICs operating with non-resident status. If the principal software sales are executed through a Vanuatu resident operating entity, however, the resident exporter must follow the standard RBV dealer rules and repatriate proceeds through a licensed commercial bank within the applicable periods for resident exporters.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Viability is rated Medium for collection acceleration and low for substantive treasury concentration. Offshore digital EMI platforms (Airwallex, Payoneer, Currencycloud-style providers) may be used as merchant-of-record or digital collection rails to aggregate Stripe Billing and Direct Debit proceeds before settlement into a licensed Vanuatu bank account. Legal constraints: such an EMI cannot accept Vatu deposits or perform Vanuatu domestic banking services without a banking licence from the RBV, and the International Company should not permit the EMI to act as the primary repository of shareholder capital or statutory corporate funds.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Tier-1 domestic banks generally mandate a physical interview for at least one executive director, beneficial owner or authorised signatory at the chosen branch or at a designated Vanuatu financial centre office. Remote video KYC may be permitted only where the bank's compliance committee approves the risk profile, and even then a licensed registered agent in Vanuatu must certify identity. During account opening, the bank will expect to sight vouched copies of the passport, proof of residential address, certified certificate of incorporation for the International Company, certificate of good standing, corporate charter, register of directors and members, registered agent acknowledgement, and bank reference letters from the parent institution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate Beneficial Owner appears on a global sanctions list, evidence-required PEP register, or adverse negative-media alert
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP clearance report, source-of-wealth sworn statement, certified passport and residential proof, professional-profile documentation, evidence of legitimate software business, bank reference letters from a regulated financial institution in the home jurisdiction, and an independent AML due-diligence opinion commissioned from a licenced compliance consultancy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border flows identified as high-chargeback software merchants under VFSC industry risk guidance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: VFSC International Company certificate, detailed commercial contracts for ERP/CRM licensing, audited or management accounts, customer KYC records, complete invoice sequence, chargeback-dispute resolution policy, product support evidence, Stripe payout history and settlement reconciliation statements, and a signed corporate policy prohibiting retail cash-collection or non-invoice revenue.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Zero-tax intragroup service fees directed to a low-tax jurisdiction without visible economic substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: OECD-aligned transfer pricing documentation covering the licence fee, intercompany service agreement, cost-and-margin build-up schedule, actual employee payroll and office substance evidence in Vanuatu or the service-provider location, annual country-by-country report, cash-flow projections, and tax-residency certificate from the home jurisdiction of the ultimate parent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Instant third-party debit pull and unidentified counterparty transfers through Direct Debit rails
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Managed customer whitelist with full KYC on each enterprise subscriber, bank account verification for all Direct Debit mandates, monthly reconciliation reports, merchant dispute monitoring, and documented transaction monitoring regular review prepared by a designated AML officer.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For the paid-up share capital injection, route funds via SWIFT MT103 from the parent or shareholder's regulated bank, using the Vanuatu International Company registration number as the remittance reference and payment descriptor 'CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION – NON-RESIDENT IC'. The receiving Vanuatu bank should classify the transaction under the international Balance of Payments convention as direct investment into an exempt international company. Supporting documents required for pre-validation include the VFSC incorporation certificate, board resolution approving the capital contribution, register of members, certified passports and address proofs of all UBOs, and confirmation from the licensed registered agent as to the non-resident status of the IC.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The operating treasury should use: (1) SWIFT MT103 for vendor invoices and partner rebates above the bank's auto-release threshold; (2) SWIFT MT101/MT102 for approved batch payroll and supplier settlements; (3) Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP-600) for high-value hardware procurement or sub-contracted development deals above USD 250,000; and (4) EMI payout engines for low-touch disbursements to software developers and cloud infrastructure vendors. For in-market recurring subscription collections, the primary rails are Stripe Billing (card) and Direct Debit (ACH/SEPA), with a daily liquidity sweep to the Vanuatu tier-1 operating account. Every outbound transfer must reference the invoice identifier and the corresponding customer or vendor AML screening record.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable VANVATU/USD outright forwards with a licensed Vanuatu bank, limited to projected receivable exposure
USD/VUV non-deliverable forward (NDF) arranged through a top-tier international dealer for long-dated licence revenue
Cross-currency swap (ISDA 2002/1992 CSA) for converting foreign-currency capital into VUV operating liquidity
European-style currency options on USD/EUR or USD/VUV floors purchased for planned ERP-cloud capital expenditures
Natural hedging by maintaining dual-currency operating accounts (VUV and USD) with daily cash-pool sweeps

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return of the International Company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the incorporation anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of approximately USD 50 per month; continued default may result in administrative strike-off and dissolution of the company

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit requirement for a Vanuatu International Company unless an audit is required by shareholders' resolution or by the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No prescribed statutory accounting framework for International Companies; internal accounting records may be maintained under IFRS or Local GAAP as a practical tax-exempt standard

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual UBO confirmation filing is required; beneficial ownership and shareholding records must be maintained at the registered agent and updated within 14 days of any share transfer or change in beneficial owner

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 - 6,000 per year if an audit is voluntarily obtained

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Vanuatu levies no corporate income tax, no capital gains tax, and no withholding tax under the Income Tax Act [Cap. 188] (repealed for domestic purposes). International Companies (ICs) are further exempted from all taxes under the International Companies Act [Cap. 222], including any future income tax, with the government issuing tax exemption certificates confirming the zero-tax status.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No corporate income tax return exists in Vanuatu for International Companies. The only filing obligations are an annual return of particulars to the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) delivered through the VFSC Online Portal / registered agent.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within one month of the anniversary of the company's registration date (or such extension granted by the VFSC).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 – Company Name and Registration Number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the International Company and its unique VFSC registration number, matching the certificate of incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter exact name as registered; a non-resident beneficial owner need not be disclosed on this public record.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 – Registered Office and Agent Details
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Physical registered office address in Vanuatu and licensed registered agent details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies must maintain the registered agent as the official communication address; no foreign business address is required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Names and addresses of directors and shareholders as maintained in the company's register; VFSC may access this in confidence.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors/shareholders may be listed; no tax residence or nationality restriction applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 – Declaration of No Taxable Activity
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration that the company has not carried on business in Vanuatu and is not liable to any tax in Vanuatu.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm that no Vanuatu-source income arises: no local real estate, no local trading, and no locally-sourced services; the company remains pure non-resident/offshore.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file the annual return/particulars with the VFSC attracts a penalty of not exceeding VT 100,000; continued default can lead to strike-off and dissolution of the company under the International Companies Act [Cap. 222], plus reinstatement costs and director disqualification risks.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Vanuatu imposes zero withholding tax on outbound dividends, interest, royalties, and management fees; therefore, no DTA relief protocol or Tax Residency Certificate application is necessary for distributions from an International Company. The corporate registrar/VFSC does not issue tax residency certificates for ICs because Vanuatu has no income tax treaty network and the company is not a Vanuatu tax resident for substantive tax purposes. Remittance of dividends is effected at the bank level without tax clearance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0% statutory; no treaty rates apply (Vanuatu has no comprehensive double tax agreements in force).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory transfer pricing documentation threshold; Vanuatu has no transfer pricing rules and no Local File/Master File regime. For substance-risk management, an International Company should maintain internal records demonstrating that the ERP/CRM cloud business is managed and directed from a jurisdiction where it has real operational substance.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Vanuatu does not administer Economic Substance Regulations similar to BVI/Cayman; no statutory economic substance test under the International Companies Act. However, entities that are managed from or that transact with entities in other jurisdictions (e.g., EU member states, OECD members) may face foreign substance requirements under the foreign entity's CFC/GILTI/controlled-foreign-company rules. To support a non-resident tax treatment, the IC must preserve board minutes, contracts, bank records, and service agreements demonstrating that core revenue-generating activities occur outside Vanuatu.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Abuse / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the International Company as a shell with no real business activity, using Vanuatu solely as a tax haven, while conducting an active ERP/CRM cloud business with overseas customers through a Vanuatu registered address only.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Vanuatu law, a company that is struck off for default can be dissolved and its assets vested in the Registrar or Crown (as applicable); knowingly providing false declarations to the VFSC attracts fines up to VT 100,000 or imprisonment. More critically, foreign tax authorities (IRS CFC, UK CFC, EU exit taxation, BEPS Action 5) may recharacterize the IC as a purely artificial offshore arrangement, imposing punitive anti-avoidance taxes and penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false declarations or allow the company to be used for tax evasion may be personally liable for fraudulent trading, disqualified from managing companies, prohibited from re-entering Vanuatu, and subject to criminal prosecution in the home jurisdiction for perjury and tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to File Annual Return / Administrative Default
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file the annual return with the VFSC, non-payment of government annual fees, or failure to maintain a licensed registered agent in Vanuatu.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Monetary penalty not exceeding VT 100,000; automatic strike-off and dissolution after continued default, with property of the company forfeited to the Crown.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be named in the strike-off notice, personally responsible for penalty arrears, banned from acting as directors in Vanuatu for up to five years, and if assets are concealed, subject to criminal confiscation orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the IC to receive or remit funds from high-risk customers without conducting AML/KYC checks, moving proceeds through Vanuatu accounts without a compliance program, or processing payments for sanctioned persons or fraud-linked digital services.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Vanuatu's Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act imposes fines up to VT 5,000,000 and imprisonment up to 15 years for non-compliance by financial institutions; beneficial-ownership reporting to the VFSC can be enforced and false filings penalized. International sanctions (FATF, UN, OFAC) may freeze assets and blacklist the corporate group.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners are personally liable for criminal penalties, including imprisonment; civil forfeiture of funds; travel bans from Vanuatu; and extradition risks for money laundering predicates.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the company to conduct domestic Vanuatu business (e.g., selling software locally, owning Vanuatu property, employing Vanuatu residents) while claiming the International Company tax exemption, or misrepresenting the company as a 'tax-free' vehicle to foreign regulators in a manner that constitutes fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax exemption is void; the company becomes subject to any Vanuatu business license fees, import duties, VAT (12.5% where applicable), and may lose its ICC status. For the exporter of services, foreign jurisdictions may impose withholding tax collections and penalty tax of 50% or more on gross revenue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly make false tax-exemption claims are liable for misrepresentation, fraudulent trading, and civil restitution to affected customers/investors; they may be criminally prosecuted and imprisoned for up to 7 years; regulatory travel bans may be issued by the VFSC and foreign enforcement agencies.
